name: Watch and jewelry repair

google_prefill.phone: [G] the listed phone (stays the business's; customers use Rosie's one number)

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)

services.name: Watch service
services.story: The main story: a watch that stopped. Only the $25 watch check is promised. Elena's written estimate is OK'd before any work, and Alex pays at the counter at pick-up, with an ID.

services.name: Battery change
services.story: A $35 watch battery change from the shop's board. Nothing is taken: a YES books it. Alex pays at the counter.

services.name: Stone replacement
services.story: A $140 stone replacement, with the stone ordered in. A $40 deposit orders it, and the $100 rest is paid at the counter.

services.name: Watch service
services.story: A watch service from $110, priced after the watch check. The $25 check is paid up front as the deposit, counted toward the final price.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer

services.name: Watch visit
services.story: The main story: a $179 watch visit (up to 5 watches: battery, band and clean) at Alex's place. A card is saved for the $89 trip fee, charged only for a late cancel or a no-show, and only on Sam's yes. Simon works alone, so the saved card is charged for the visit when Simon texts DONE.

services.name: Watch visit
services.story: The same $179 watch visit. A card is saved for the $89 trip fee. Rosie texts the bill after.

services.name: Jewelry repair
services.story: A broken clasp and a loose stone, priced at the visit. A card is saved for the $89 trip fee.

services.name: Ring repair
services.story: A custom ring repair, priced from photos of the ring at $640. Sam OKs it. A $160 deposit orders the parts, and the rest is on the bill.

What's wrong: stopped, battery, loose band, cracked crystal, wrong size, broken clasp, loose stone, or something else
Is it a gift, an heirloom or insured?
For a visit at the customer's place: a home or an office, and the address
license: none for repair itself; the business registration, where the city or state asks for one; a precious metals or secondhand dealer license only if the shop buys gold or used jewelry, where the city or state requires one
